title: Lena and the Sigil
premise: Ines Underhill, youngest keeper of the Ledgerwrights—a guild that trades in impossible things—has spent her life recording bargains she was never allowed to make. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive in the port city of Vell and the guild's last elders scatter or die, Ines inherits both the ledgers and the sigil that opens the Hollow Door: the only passage out of a country being erased by an old treaty no one remembers signing. Hunted alongside a disgraced royal cartographer, Tomas, whose maps can find what should not exist, she must trade her own name—the one thing she owns—to open the door. She does, but chooses to stay behind with Tomas and the guild's remnant, sealing the door so the hunted can escape while she rebuilds the guild as something new, its inheritance carried forward rather than fled from.
about_author: Paloma Nystrom is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing merchant records in Baltic port towns before turning to fiction. Her novels blend meticulous historical texture with quiet, stubborn magic.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Debts
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Ines catalogs the guild's dwindling inventory of impossible goods while the elders argue over unpaid debts to the crown. A child trades a memory for bread, and Ines secretly records it under her own name. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as diligence; her longing to matter within a dying institution.

chapters.title: Proclamation at the Fish Gate
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The crown posts a decree: all gifted persons must register or be taken. An elder burns half the ledger to hide names, then dies of a stroke mid-argument. Ines pockets the sigil he drops. Emotional beat: fear hardening into resolve; the moment invisibility stops being safety.

chapters.title: What the Map Remembers
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Disgraced cartographer Tomas Vey is caught drawing a street that officially never existed. Fleeing hunters, he stumbles into the guildhall through a door that shouldn't be there. He and Ines recognize each other's dangerous talents. Emotional beat: wary kinship between two people trained to erase themselves.

chapters.title: Inventory of Ghosts
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Reading the oldest ledger, Ines learns the guild once brokered the treaty that erased the neighboring country of Sarn—and that the Hollow Door out of it still answers to their sigil. The price of opening it has always been a true name freely given. Emotional beat: horror at inherited complicity; grief braided with purpose.

chapters.title: The Hunter Who Smiles
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Witch-hunter Captain Aldous Renn interrogates the city, courteous and patient, using a compass that points toward gifts rather than north. He nearly catches Ines; Tomas misdirects him with a forged map at real cost—a friend is taken. Emotional beat: guilt, and the first blood on their hands.

chapters.title: A Bargain in the Salt Cellar
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The remaining guild members vote to flee through the Door, but it will only open where Sarn used to be—in the drowned quarter beyond the harbor wall. Ines must bargain with a tide-wight for safe passage, offering memories of her mother. Emotional beat: love against duty; she pays willingly and feels smaller for it.

chapters.title: Renn's Offer
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Renn corners Tomas privately and offers clemency in exchange for the sigil, revealing the hunt is really about reclaiming the Door for the crown's own exiles. Tomas pretends to consider, buying time but planting doubt. Emotional beat: temptation of survival through betrayal; Tomas's loyalty crystallizes into love he won't say aloud.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. The harbor freezes unnaturally early—Renn's doing, sealing the drowned quarter. With the tide-wight's route closed, Ines realizes the Door must be opened from inside the guildhall itself, which means someone must stay to hold it. Emotional beat: despair transfigured into clarity; she understands what inheritance truly costs.

chapters.title: The Hollow Door
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax. Renn storms the guildhall as Ines gives her true name to the sigil and Tomas anchors the Door with his impossible map. The hunted pour through as the hall burns; Renn reaches for Ines across the threshold and is refused—the Door knows a freely given thing when it sees one. Emotional beat: sacrifice answered by grace.

chapters.title: Ledgerwright
chapters.summary: Ines's POV. Resolution. The Door sealed behind the refugees, Ines and Tomas remain in a country learning to remember Sarn again. She founds a new ledger—not of trades, but of names restored—and writes herself on the first page. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited; winter ending.
